archetypes.title: Prince's Island Park
archetypes.description: River island park in the Bow River with walking paths, cottonwood trees, public art, event lawns, and mountain views

Large manicured grass lawns, ponds with fountains, flower gardens, art sculptures, outdoor stage, children's playground. Network of trails lined with cottonwood trees. Eastern end is designated wetland marsh (Chevron Learning Pathway). Connected to downtown by three bridges. Integrated into Bow River Pathway system. Mountain views on clear days.

archetypes.title: Halifax Public Gardens
archetypes.description: One of the finest surviving Victorian gardens in North America with bandstand, carpet beds, serpentine paths, and wrough

styleProfile.landscapeCharacter: 16-acre National Historic Site. Founded 1836. Gardenesque landscape by Richard Power. Axially symmetrical plan. Serpentine paths. Geometric carpet beds (densely planted dwarf plants in contrasting colours). Bandstand (1887, Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee). Three fountains. Two stone bridges. Three ponds. Wrought-iron gates. Mature deciduous trees. Commemorative statuary. Enclosed by iron fence — bounded, curated space.
styleProfile.pavingType: Serpentine gravel and stone paths in formal layout
styleProfile.plantingType: Geometric carpet beds with contrasting plants, mature deciduous trees, tropical display beds (Victorian tradition)
styleProfile.seatingRealm: Wrought-iron benches, bandstand (1887), commemorative statuary, stone bridges over ponds
styleProfile.waterFeatures: Three fountains, three ponds with stone bridges, formal water features
styleProfile.opennessEnclosure: Semi-enclosed

archetypes.title: Halifax Coastal Forest Park
archetypes.description: Coastal forest park meeting the Atlantic Ocean with hiking trails, ruined fortifications, rocky shoreline, and salt-wind

styleProfile.landscapeCharacter: Coastal forest park at the tip of the Halifax peninsula. Mixed forest meeting the Atlantic Ocean. Hiking trails through woods. Ruined stone fortifications (18th-century batteries and towers). Rocky shoreline. Salt spray and wind shape the vegetation. Wilder and more exposed character than urban parks. Regenerating forest (much lost to Hurricane Juan in 2003).
styleProfile.pavingType: Unpaved hiking trails through forest, some gravel paths
styleProfile.plantingType: Mixed coastal forest: spruce, birch, maple. Salt-wind shaped trees. Regenerating understory.
styleProfile.seatingRealm: Simple trail markers, wooden benches at viewpoints, interpretive panels at fortification ruins
styleProfile.waterFeatures: Atlantic Ocean at shoreline, tidal pools on rocky coast
styleProfile.opennessEnclosure: Semi-enclosed
